review.note:
Setup and cleanup blocks ran verbatim and succeeded (cleanup left change.patch and inputs.json in /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/build/review-1-opus). I reviewed the whole change 1bebd14..d004f80 against the frozen PRD and spec views, and found no defect the implementation rubric allows me to report.

What I checked in the code:
- src/login.js handler order follows DEC-003 and DEC-010: validation, then the arrival check(), then gate.run(). Inside the gate task, begin() runs before users.has, verifyAsync or the dummy hashPasswordAsync.
- A 503 changes no limiter state.
- end() runs on both the success and the reject path, and a rejected verification answers 500 without counting as a failure.
- The gate releases its slot in finally before the response, and queued tasks start in FIFO order.
- Retry-After is ceil((oldest + 60000 - now) / 1000) when 5 timestamps remain, and 1 when the lock is due to in-flight attempts.
- The session store and the limiter are each capped at 10000: expired, idle records are pruned first, then the oldest record is evicted.
- The body cap is 4096 bytes and returns 413 with connection: close; validation is 1..64 characters for username and 1..1024 for password, otherwise 400.
- The bodies are the fixed DEC-005 ones, and the 503 body is the 401 body.
- The dummy hash is read from the users module object at call time, as DEC-004 requires.
- src/users.js only adds hashPasswordAsync and verifyAsync; the existing exports are unchanged.
- src/server.js keeps GET /health, the 404 fallback and the existing options.
- A grep for console or process.stdout/stderr in src/*.js finds only the existing 'listening on' line.

The new tests cover every acceptance criterion I looked at.

Observed: npm test in the review worktree reported 32 tests, 32 pass, 0 fail. I did not run any proof command from the canonical feature file.

Two things I looked at and decided not to report:
- When the limiter is full, it can evict a record that still has an attempt in verification. This is within accepted risk RISK-002.
- Once the limiter holds 10000 live records, pruning in track() scans all of them for each new username. That is bounded by the gate and costs far less than one scrypt call.

security.note:
Independent security review (opus-high fallback for Codex) of 1bebd14b..d004f807, covering src/login.js, src/server.js, src/users.js, README.md and the tests. I read the code in the isolated worktree /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/build/security-1-opus/wt (Node v22.23.4). Setup and cleanup ran as given. The worktree is removed and /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/build/security-1-opus is left empty. I changed no files and executed no tests or spec commands. The test suite was NOT RUN.

No critical or high findings.

What I checked:
- Input validation and size limits (API4). readBody counts bytes, stops buffering once the body is over 4096 bytes (`if (size > limit) { chunks.length = 0; resolve(null); }`), and the handler then answers 413 with connection: close. parseCredentials accepts only a plain object with string username (1..64 characters) and password (1..1024 characters). Invalid input is rejected before the limiter, the gate or any hashing.
- Injection and deserialization. The only parser is JSON.parse. The username is used only as a Map key, so `__proto__` cannot pollute the prototype, and it is never echoed back. No file paths, outbound requests, eval or shell are involved.
- Brute force and race conditions. limiter.check on arrival is followed by limiter.begin inside the gate task, and `record.timestamps.length + record.pending < maxFailures` counts attempts in flight. Concurrent or queued attempts therefore cannot exceed 5 verifications per username per 60 seconds. A successful login does not reset the count. Unknown usernames get the same lockout.
- Expensive operation. scrypt now runs on the libuv threadpool, behind a gate shared by the whole server (4 running, 16 queued, otherwise 503 with no hashing). Every Map is capped: limiter records at 10000, each holding at most 5 timestamps, and sessions at 10000.
- User enumeration. Unknown users get `hashPasswordAsync(password, DUMMY_SALT)` under the gate. The 401 body is identical for unknown users and wrong passwords, and the 503 reuses it. The 503 is decided before the username is looked up.
- Secrets and logging. The token is `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')`. The changed code logs nothing, and the 500 paths return a fixed body.
- Authorization (API1/3/5). No endpoint consumes the token yet. Same-origin content calling /login gains nothing beyond what any client has: no ambient credentials or cookies are used, and the token comes back only in the response body.

Medium issues, not blocking. All of these are already recorded as accepted risks in the feature spec:
- RISK-001: a flood with rotating usernames fills the server-wide gate, so legitimate logins get 503. There is no limit per IP.
- RISK-002: flooding the limiter with more than 10000 usernames can evict a record and end a lockout early. At gate throughput this does not raise the guess rate against a target.
- RISK-003: anyone can keep a known username locked out.
- RISK-004: small timing differences remain between the unknown-user and wrong-password paths.
- RISK-005: tokens never expire. One user with valid credentials can log in repeatedly and push other users' sessions out of the 10000 cap.

Low, not blocking:
- The 200 token response sends no `cache-control: no-store` (`sendJson(res, 200, { token: sessions.issue(username) })`).
- How long a slow body upload can take is limited only by Node's default request timeouts.

work.summary:
I built session-login test-first on feat/session-login-r3 and pushed the branch to origin (ee05971..d004f80). The focused tests failed on assertions at the RED commit and pass at the final commit.

RED commit f293a35d2ea498cad8faf9cb47b2003ba6c1bcae adds only the six test files listed in scope.test_paths. Running the focused-test command there exited 1: 27 tests, 0 passed, 27 failed. All 27 failed with ERR_ASSERTION and failureType 'testCodeFailure', so none were crashes, timeouts or missing modules (each file loads src/login.js lazily so a missing module fails an assertion instead of the whole file). The 5 existing tests in health and users still passed.

GREEN commit d004f807efbc39d004b3fe4352351c8dba3a9177 adds the implementation:
- New src/login.js: the session store (capped at 10000 tokens), the per-username sliding-window limiter (attempts still being verified count toward the lock; capped at 10000 usernames), the server-wide verification gate (4 running, 16 waiting, 503 beyond that), the login handler, and the constants from DEC-001.
- src/users.js: two additions, hashPasswordAsync and store.verifyAsync. Existing exports are unchanged.
- src/server.js: routes POST /login and takes optional sessions, now and gate settings. GET /health and the 404 fallback are unchanged.
- README.md: a short POST /login section.

At the final commit the focused-test command exited 0 (27 passed, 0 failed, about 4.0 s), and npm test exited 0 (32 passed, 0 failed).

Mutation spot checks: I applied 7 of the spec's mutations to src/login.js one at a time and put the file back after each (cmp confirmed it matches). All 7 were caught (exit 1): no queue limit, allowing a 5th active verification (`<=` instead of `<`), lock ignoring in-flight attempts, failures never recorded, constant token, dummy hash removed, and slot freed only when verification succeeds. The queue-limit and `<=` mutations each took about 20 s to fail because a request stays parked until the 20 s test timeout. That is still well under the 120 s proof timeout. My first try at the in-flight mutation used the wrong search text and ran unmutated (exit 0); the retry with the right text exited 1. The dummy-hash check deleted the call rather than moving it outside the gate as the spec describes, so it only approximates that mutation. I did not run the other 21 mutations.

LOGIN-006-AC3 is static: the six test files exist under test/ and match the package.json glob. The staged diffs were scanned for secrets before both commits and nothing was found. Saved outputs are in /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/build/implement/: red.txt, green.txt and npm-test.txt.
